candidates.label: Konya (ancient Iconium)
candidates.support: The modern city of Konya overlies ancient Iconium continuously; the identification is undisputed and Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the site agree closely.

summary.text: Iconium was a city of Lycaonia (later administratively linked with Galatia) that Paul and Barnabas visited on the first missionary journey, preaching in its synagogue before opposition drove them on to Lystra.

history.text: Ancient writers disagreed on whether Iconium belonged to Phrygia or Lycaonia. The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia notes that 'the majority of our ancient authorities (e.g. Cicero, Strabo, Pliny), writing from the point of view of Roman provincial administration, give Iconium to Lycaonia,' but that Xenophon 'calls Iconium the last city of Phrygia,' and that Acts 14:6 implies the same, by describing Paul and Barnabas as fleeing from Iconium to 'the cities of Lycaonia,' Lystra and Derbe. The same source concludes that in the apostolic period Iconium was 'one of the chief cities in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia,' and that it probably belonged to the 'Phrygian region' of Acts 16:6. Either way it lay in the province of Galatia, which this project gives as its parent.

scripture.textWEB: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to Iconium.
In Iconium, they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.
But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
When they had preached the Good News to that city and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
The brothers who were at Lystra and Iconium gave a good testimony about him.
persecutions, and sufferings—those things that happened to me at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. I endured those persecutions. The Lord delivered me out of them all.
